# How does an old tree get its bark?

<!-- STEP id="young" -->
## A young stem
In young plants, the outer protective layer is the epidermis, a single layer of cells. As a tree grows older and its trunk gets thicker, one thin layer is no longer enough to cover it.

<!-- STEP id="cambium" -->
## Cork cambium
As plants grow older, some cells below the epidermis of the stem develop the ability to divide. They act as a lateral meristem and form the cork cambium. These are living permanent cells that start dividing again, as the previous lesson said some can.

<!-- STEP id="cork" -->
## Cork cells
The cork cambium divides to make cork cells. Cork cells are dead and tightly packed, and they contain a substance that stops water and gases from passing through. These layers of cork form the bark of the tree.

**Bark is a protective layer of dead cork cells, made by the cork cambium.**
